headline: Stocks and Currency Both Fall: New Taiwan Dollar Depreciates 8 Cents, Weekly Losses for a Second Consecutive Week | Industry & Finance
summary: The New Taiwan dollar closed at 31.875 per US dollar, down 8 cents, for a second weekly loss. Stocks also fell as Middle East tensions, a spike in US Treasury yields and hawkish Fed minutes weighed on risk appetite.
why: The New Taiwan dollar is the currency of Taiwan, whose stock market is a major global hub for semiconductor shares, so currency and equity moves reflect global risk sentiment.

impacts.name: New Taiwan dollar
impacts.why: The currency closed down 8 cents against the US dollar at 31.875, its second consecutive weekly loss.

why_moved: Rising Middle East tensions, a spike in US Treasury yields and hawkish signals in the US Federal Reserve meeting minutes reduced risk appetite. Hot money outflows then pushed both stocks and the currency lower.
